{{Short description|English logician}}
'''Alexander Richardson''' (c1565-1613?) was an English [[logician]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://quod.lib.umich.edu/e/eebo2/A91783.0001.001/1:6.6.8?rgn=div3;view=fulltext|title=The logicians school-master: or, A comment upon Ramus logick.: By Mr. Alexander Richardson|access-date=2023-01-17}}</ref>

== Life ==
Richardson was a Master of Arts at [[Queens' College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://quod.lib.umich.edu/e/eebo2/A91783.0001.001/1:2?rgn=div1;view=fulltext|title=The logicians school-master: or, A comment upon Ramus logick.: By Mr. Alexander Richardson|access-date=2023-01-17}}</ref>  He also tutored at [[George Walker (Puritan)|George Walker]]'s house in Barking, Essex.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kennedy |first1=Rick and Thomas Knoles |title=Increase Mather's 'Catechismus Logicus': A Translation and an Analysis of the Role of a Ramist Catechism at Harvard |journal=Proceedings of the American Antiquarian Society |date=1999 |volume=109 |page=155}}</ref>

== Works ==
Richardson wrote a logic textbook in the [[Ramism|Ramist]] tradition, ''The logicians school-master: or, A comment upon Ramus logick.: By Mr. Alexander Richardson, sometime of Queenes Colledge in Cambridge. Whereunto are added, his prelections on Ramus his grammer; Taleus his rhetorick; also his notes on physicks, ethicks, astronomy, medicine, and opticks.''  The book was first published in London in 1629 and enlarged in 1657.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kennedy |first1=Rick and Thomas Knoles |title=Increase Mather's 'Catechismus Logicus': A Translation and an Analysis of the Role of a Ramist Catechism at Harvard |journal=Proceedings of the American Antiquarian Society |date=1999 |volume=109 |page=155}}</ref>
